The Authentic Name

Why tārā.com is the correct form

Devanagari

तारा

The name in its original Devanagari form. तारा → Tārā. Sanskrit Tārā is written in Devanagari as तारा · IAST transliteration maps each Devanagari vowel and consonant to a Latin equivalent · Macrons mark long vowels (ā, ī, ū); dots beneath consonants mark retroflex articulation (ṭ, ḍ, ṇ, ṣ)

ASCII Constraint

TARA

Stripped of its identity, the name was reduced to plain Latin letters. The original orthography — stress, length, breathing — was erased by systems that only understand A-Z.

Unicode Restoration

Tārā

The Unicode restoration recovers what ASCII destroyed. This is philological accuracy — not decoration. The domain encodes to Punycode, but the browser displays the truth.

Punycode Encoding
tārā.com → xn--tr-dlab.com

The non-ASCII characters in Tārā are encoded while the ASCII remains visible. To the DNS, it is Punycode. To humanity, it is Tārā.

Tier Classification

Why Tārā is classified as Tier-1 Macron-Preserving

The Ancient name तारा is represented by its most canonical scholarly spelling. For non-Greek names, Tier-1 status reflects the definitive attested restoration rather than Greek-style stress/length features. This is the authoritative Unicode form — a single-tier Tier-1 name.
